summary: Native addon exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials to attacker host on require()
details: The package is a thin NestJS 'archetype' stub (empty forRoot/createLogger exports) published at version 999.0.1 under a scope resembling an internal toolkit name — the shape of a dependency-confusion squat. On require(), index.js resolves prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node and loads it inside a try/catch, executing opaque native code at module load; no binding.gyp or source is shipped, so the ELF is the sole payload. The native binary reads high-value CI/cloud environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN) together with hostname, uid, cwd, and uname, and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded external host oob.s4yhii.com (POST /native HTTP/1.0), using fork+setsid to detach the exfil process. Any build or CI pipeline that resolves and imports this package has its cloud, GitHub Actions, and npm publishing credentials shipped to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
